Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking our RFI. Attached is the worksheet we use to map lineage, license obligations, and permitted uses for any model we consider deploying. Can you complete sections 1–4 and return by EOD Thursday (48 hours)? Key asks:

- Canonical license for each model in your public catalog (including any dual-license cases)
- Whether downstream commercial/redistribution rights are allowed for derivatives
- What provenance metadata you supply (hashes, source snapshot, training-data indicators)
- Your recommended pinning strategy and typical notification/deprecation windows

We have some follow-ups in the security questionnaire but wanted to get this matrix first. If you prefer a short attestation PDF instead of filling the spreadsheet, that would work too — please include contact for legal redlines.

Subject: Re: AcmeCloud RFI — Model Lineage & Usage Rights Questionnaire

Amanda — thanks for the spreadsheet. We're happy to return that completed; attaching two artifacts we typically provide to customers that cover most of your asks: a compact attestation and our license mapping.

Summary (high level):
- License mapping: public catalog models are annotated with the model license (e.g., MIT, Apache-2.0, Creative Commons BY-SA, custom permissive). Dual-license cases are flagged and we supply the upstream license text. See attached License-Matrix.csv for examples.
- Redistribution/derivatives: Permitted uses follow the source license unless otherwise noted in the model entry. For models with share-alike terms we call out restrictions explicitly. Commercial use is allowed for X% of catalog; exceptions noted in the matrix.
- Provenance metadata: For each model we provide model_id, semantic version, exact checkpoint hash (SHA256), origin repo URL or upstream release tag, and a timestamped import snapshot. For models we fine-tuned, we include a short training-notes field and any third-party datasets used (high level).
- Pinning & updates: Customers can pin to a model_id+version hash. We publish an update channel and provide deprecation notice windows: standard models: 30 days; major breaking changes: 90 days; security-critical fixes: emergency patch with immediate notice and optional forced rollback window. Our compact attestation covers the recommended pinning policy and rollback controls.

Next steps:
1) Do you want us to complete the attached spreadsheet or is the attestation PDF sufficient?
2) If legal wants to redline the attestation, point us to the contact and we'll loop in our legal lead.

Attachments: Redwood_Model-Lineage-Attestation.pdf (pdf), License-Matrix.csv (csv)

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference

3) For our security team: do you provide cryptographic provenance (signed manifest) that we can verify independently?

Also, could you provide a legal contact for attestation redlines and a DocuSign link if you have a standard attestation?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: AcmeCloud RFI — Model Lineage & Usage Rights Questionnaire

Amanda — thanks for the follow-ups. I'm Karthik on our product/legal/safety coordination team; copying Neha (legal) for any contract language. Brief answers below and links to artifacts.

1) Third-party-weighted training data and redistribution:
- Our platform enforces the open-source license of the upstream model. If the upstream license permits redistribution and commercial use, downstream checkpoints are allowed. For models that include datasets with additional contractual constraints, we surface those constraints in the model entry and in the License-Matrix.csv.
- We provide an explicit "redistribution_rights" field in the model metadata (values: full, derivative-only, prohibited) you can consume programmatically via the catalog API.

2) Upstream license changes & notification:
- We monitor upstream repos and releases. When a license change is detected, customers pinned to the older model_id+hash are notified immediately via email and in-console banner.
- Deprecation policy: if the change affects permitted use, we recommend migration; standard non-security license changes follow a 30-day notice, but for breaking license changes we extend to a 90-day migration window and offer engineering support for pin migration. These windows are included in the attestation PDF and in our SLA addendum for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.

3) Cryptographic provenance:
- Yes. We publish a signed manifest (Ed25519) for each published model version that includes the SHA256 of the checkpoint, origin URL, import timestamp, and an audit_log_id. You can verify the signature with our public key (rotated quarterly). Example verify flow is in our developer docs.

Legal & attestation logistics:
- Neha Kapoor (neha.kapoor@redwood.ai) is our commercial counsel and will review any redlines.
- We also host a DocuSign attestation for standard customers; quick link attached in a stub file for procurement to consume.

Links & artifacts:
- Public catalog: https://redwood.ai/catalog
- Attestation record: https://redwood.ai/attestations/ACME-4871
- Quick DocuSign (attestation): https://docusign.com/xyz (one-click)

Attachments: Attestation_Docusign_Link.txt (link stub)

If you want, Ben can schedule a short technical session to walk security through the signed-manifest verification and the catalog API.

Best regards,
